solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Something beneficial, like radio, for example?

parts.note: as means like, in the way of
a radio is one kind of set, a receiving apparatus

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a radio counts as something useful to own.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that radio is only an example of a set, as in a radio set.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a valuable or useful thing or quality is called a plus in one's favour.

clue.text: A professional performer rates it badly

indicators.note: badly signals the words rates it are put together poorly, i.e. rearranged

explanation.surface: A critic gives a poor review of a stage professional's act.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a professional entertainer such as a singer or dancer, from the French word for artist.

clue.text: Party attended by mountaineer, one seeking status?

indicators.note: attended by means accompanied by, so one piece is followed by the next

parts.note: a social is an informal party or gathering
a mountaineer is a climber

explanation.surface: A mountaineer turns up at a party, perhaps hoping to impress.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a person anxious to rise in society and gain prestige among those above them.

clue.text: Monks ensnare last of animals in deep holes

parts.note: to trap is to ensnare

indicators.note: in places the picked letter within the holes

parts.note: pits are deep holes

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of the word animals

explanation.surface: Monks catch animals by trapping them in pits.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Trappists are a Cistercian order of monks noted for their vow of silence.

clue.text: Old man holding end of mauve quill

indicators.note: holding means one piece contains another

parts.note: old man is informal for one's father

indicators.note: end of takes the final letter of the word mauve

explanation.surface: An elderly gentleman holds a pen with a purple tip.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a quill is a large bird's plume, the kind once used as a pen.

clue.text: Gaudy insect circling tree

indicators.note: circling means the insect goes round the tree, enclosing it

parts.note: a fly is an insect
the ash is a tree

explanation.surface: A brightly coloured insect buzzes round a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: ostentatious and showy in a cheap or tasteless way.

clue.text: Help! The opera isn't finished!

indicators.note: isn't finished means the opera's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Aida is the famous opera by Verdi

explanation.surface: An alarmed cry from someone whose opera is incomplete.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: assistance or support, here as a call for rescue.

clue.text: Tree Arab, say, associated with old joke

parts.note: an Arab is a breed of horse
a chestnut is a stale, often-told joke

explanation.surface: Someone from Arabia is linked with a tired old gag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arab' looks like a person, but here it is the horse breed.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a large deciduous tree bearing conkers, common in parks.

clue.text: Competition for ethnic group

definitions.meaning: a contest of speed, as on a track
a people sharing descent or ancestry

explanation.surface: A contest held for one ethnic community.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a speed contest, and a group of people of common descent.

clue.text: Piece that's unusually staccato — not Schubert's first

indicators.note: unusually signals the letters of staccato are arranged in an unusual order
first picks the opening letter of the composer's name

explanation.surface: A musical work played in a strangely detached style, though not Schubert's opening one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes the S (Schubert's first) from STACCATO before the rest is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a toccata is a virtuoso keyboard composition, a musical work.

clue.text: Like some architecture in Greenland or Iceland?

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit within the words Greenland or Iceland

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about building styles found in the far north.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: one of the classical Greek orders of columns, plain and sturdy.

clue.text: Skilled marksman notes owl

parts.note: sharps are musical notes raised a semitone
an owl is a hooter, from its call

explanation.surface: An expert shot takes note of an owl, perhaps as a target.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone who shoots with great accuracy.

clue.text: Unemployed old female in dated composition

indicators.note: in places the two letters inside the other pieces

parts.note: out can mean out of fashion, dated
a work is a composition, as in music

explanation.surface: An elderly woman appears in an old-fashioned piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: having no job, jobless.

clue.text: Cut out PE without hesitation

indicators.note: without means taking the hesitation sound away

parts.note: PE, physical education, is exercise
er is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A school drops gym lessons without a second thought.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to remove surgically or delete a passage.

clue.text: Cockney's mention of 'old-ups is irritating

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker traditionally drops the initial h of words

parts.note: hold-ups, written as a Cockney would say it, are hitches

explanation.surface: A Londoner complains that delays are annoying.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the working-class East London accent, famous for dropping the h; the clue shows this in 'old-ups.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a part of the body that tingles annoyingly makes one want to scratch.

clue.text: Reliably do silly manoeuvres

indicators.note: manoeuvres signals the letters of do silly are moved around

explanation.surface: An instruction to perform daft manoeuvres in a dependable way.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: in a dependable, firm and steady manner.

clue.text: Emergency primarily concerning river, the one in Oxford

indicators.note: primarily takes the first letter of the word concerning

parts.note: the Isis is the name given to the Thames as it flows through Oxford

explanation.surface: An urgent situation involving the river that runs through Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a time of acute danger or difficulty.

clue.text: Preferential treatment getting showjumper off to a bad start?

definitions.meaning: the right to be offered something before others are

definitions.text: showjumper off to a bad start?
definitions.meaning: a horse balking at the opening fence

explanation.surface: A rider gets special favours after a poor opening round.
explanation.walkthrough: In showjumping, a refusal is a horse stopping at a jump; one at the opening fence is a bad start.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the chance to accept or decline an offer before it goes to anyone else.

clue.text: Powder stored in metal cupboard

indicators.note: stored in says the letters are kept within the words metal cupboard

explanation.surface: Some powder is kept in a steel cabinet.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a soft mineral ground into a fine powder for the skin.

clue.text: Scope of non-grammatical complaint after dog attack?

definitions.meaning: the range or extent of something
an ungrammatical moan of a victim saying they were bitten

explanation.surface: Someone bitten by a dog grumbles in poor grammar about their range.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits as AM BIT, a broken-English way to say 'I was bitten'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the bounds or range of influence of something.

clue.text: Old books brought up in addition

indicators.note: brought up in a down clue means read from bottom to top

parts.note: OT, the Old Testament, is a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Old volumes are mentioned as well.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: also, besides, as well.

clue.text: Scoffed at sailors visiting southern school

indicators.note: visiting means the sailors go inside

parts.note: coed is a coeducational school
RN, the Royal Navy, stands for sailors

explanation.surface: Sailors call at a school in the south and get mocked.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: treated with contempt, derided.

clue.text: Contemptible scoundrel promises to pay? Strange

parts.note: a cur is a worthless, contemptible man
IOUs are written promises to pay a debt

explanation.surface: A rogue hands out debt notes, which seems odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: odd, peculiar, out of the ordinary.

clue.text: Pool of money for cat?

definitions.meaning: a shared fund that people pay into
a pet name for a cat or kitten

explanation.surface: A collection is taken up for a pet cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a communal fund of stakes, and an affectionate name for a cat.
